title: Curried Mince Pie
subtitle: A spiced minced beef filling baked inside a shortcrust pastry case
excerpt: Minced beef cooked with onion, ginger, garlic and warm spices, baked inside a short pastry case. A British-Indian kitchen classic.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian home cooking tradition combining a dry curried mince with shortcrust pastry.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to two days ahead. The spices deepen overnight.

content.text: The mince filling is cooked dry so there is no excess liquid to soften the pastry base. Get it properly coloured and fragrant before it goes into the pie. Cool the filling to room temperature before assembling.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring often. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 1 minute.
Add the mince. Break it apart and stir over a high heat until browned all over, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the tinned tomatoes and salt. Cook uncovered over a medium heat for 15 minutes until the mixture is dry. Stir in the garam masala and fresh coriander. Leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish. Spoon in the cooled filling.
Roll the remaining pastry into a lid. Brush the rim with egg, press on the lid and crimp. Brush with egg and cut two slits.
Bake for 35 minutes until the pastry is deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: The base is soggy after baking.
items.cause: The filling was too wet when it went into the pastry.
items.fix: Cook the filling until completely dry and no liquid pools at the bottom of the pan.

items.cause: The ground spices were not cooked in the oil long enough.
items.fix: Stir the spices with the onion mixture for a full minute before adding the mince.

items.symptom: The pastry edges shrink away from the dish.
items.cause: The pastry was stretched rather than pressed in when lining the dish.
items.fix: Lay the pastry gently into the dish without pulling. Let any excess hang over the edge before trimming.
